advisor_identified: Historian of modern Britain and professor in McGill University's Department of History and Classical Studies.

doctorate.title: Bourgeois Ideology and Order: Middle-Class Culture and Politics in Lancashire, 1789-1851

evidence.says: McGill identifies Lewis as a professor and historian of modern Britain and lists PhD (Harvard). He explains that The Middlemost and the Milltowns grew out of his doctoral thesis on middle-class culture and politics in Lancashire cotton towns, 1789-1851.

Stephanie Olsen's institution-hosted CV, page 1, lists her 2003-2008 McGill doctorate, Raising Fathers, Raising Boys: Informal Education and Enculturation in Britain, 1880-1914, with Brian Lewis among its supervisors, matching a student dissertation in this entry.

The library catalogue record for Brian Lewis's The Middlemost and the Milltowns (Stanford University Press, 2001) states that it was originally presented as the author's PhD thesis at Harvard University.

The repository thesis's indexed bibliography, page 293, cites Brian Lewis, Bourgeois Ideology and Order: Middle-Class Culture and Politics in Lancashire, 1789-1851, as a PhD thesis in History, Harvard University, 1994.

notes: The institution, subject and period match the linked record. The exact title and 1994 date are corroborated by a scholarly bibliography; a catalogue record of the dissertation itself was not located. The repository PDF could not be fetched directly, so its bibliographic citation was checked through indexed text.
